rawFindings.claim: Phase 0.5 exit gate now requires proving Host-owned Agent-replacement semantics, but the phase's scope, deliverables, and required tests define no Host/Agent-Protocol work
rawFindings.description: This PR edits the authoritative §0.5 exit gate in docs/phase-0-spec.md to require that 'Agent replacement/restart does not invalidate Host-owned execution identity or durable state — the Host supervises the Agent, so replacing or restarting the Agent process preserves operation identity, session state, and canonical events.' However, the rest of §0.5 was left in the old framing: its implementation scope is only the extensions/cognition adapter + packages/cognition-runtime coordinator split, lifecycle mapping, and agent-callable tools; its deliverables and required tests (integration, crash, concurrency) contain no Host supervisor, Agent Protocol, agent process restart, or Host-owned execution identity items. The 'Host' control-plane concept is defined only in the new docs/roadmap.md, which itself declares that 'the executable specification with authoritative gate definitions lives in phase-0-spec.md' and that the Agent Protocol 'starts here' at 0.5. Per docs/rules.md and constitution principle 10, a gate is passed only when its executable command emits status:'passed' — so the authoritative gate now embeds a check whose subject (Host supervision, agent replacement) is not built, tested, or even defined within the authoritative spec. When gate:0.5 is implemented it will be undefined what operationally proves this clause, or the clause will be silently unenforceable. Fix by either adding the Host supervision/Agent-restart scope and test items to §0.5, or moving this clause out of the executable gate text.

proof.summary: Static trace: read §0.5 in full at HEAD — exit gate (changed lines 541-551) references 'Host-owned execution identity' and Agent process replacement, while the section's implementation scope, deliverables, and required tests (ending at line 539) contain no Host/Agent-replacement work items; a repo-wide search for 'Host owns' matches only docs/roadmap.md (line 197), the non-authoritative orientation doc.

rawFindings.claim: Triage decision log can now report decision:'skipped' for issues where the worker actually acted (posted a comment and created a managed add-comment action)
rawFindings.description: The PR changes the comment gate from `needs_more_info || duplicate_hint` to `auto_comment !== false`, so every successfully triaged issue now posts a comment and runs the propose/approve/execute/succeed action-state-machine sequence. However, the decision log written just before the comment block still derives its `decision` value solely from `labelsToApply.length` ('acted'/'dry_run' only when labels were applied, otherwise 'skipped') and its `conditions`/`configUsed` only mention `auto_label` — `auto_comment` is never recorded. Before this change the inconsistency was limited to needs_more_info/duplicate issues with no matching labels; after this change every issue that gets labels filtered out (or has auto_label:false, e.g. test 6 in the new test file) will be logged as 'skipped / no labels to apply' even though a public GitHub comment and a managed add-comment action were created. This weakens the audit trail this repo otherwise maintains rigorously (cf. wave2 writer audit, decision-log attribution work). Not a functional break, but worth aligning the decision log with the new always-comment behavior.

proof.summary: Verified at HEAD: the logDecision block (lines ~334-347) computes decision from labelsToApply.length only and records configUsed { auto_label } with no auto_comment entry, while the immediately following block (lines 349-414) now unconditionally posts a comment and creates a managed action when auto_comment !== false. Line 340 (conditions[0]) and 345 (configUsed) were confirmed by direct read; 337 (decision line) derived from the same verified anchor.

It never re-invokes triageIssue a second time, so the 'exactly one comment, updated not duplicated' retry contract advertised in the new code comment is not exercised end-to-end (including the re-propose of actionKey triage:comment:issue:N on retry). The happy path coverage is otherwise solid (normal issue posts comment, auto_comment:false suppresses it, needs_more_info section present, dry-run suppresses, footer truthful).

proof.summary: Test body issues a single triageIssue call with postMarkedComment mocked to resolve {action:'updated'}; no second invocation exists, so no retry/idempotency behavior is actually asserted.

rawFindings.claim: findCommentByMarker's JSDoc return contract is now inaccurate: it documents { ambiguous: true, comments: [] } but the implementation returns the matched comments
rawFindings.description: The rewritten findCommentByMarker returns { ambiguous: true, comments: matches } on both the new early-exit path (>= 2 matches found mid-pagination) and the post-loop tail, but the @returns JSDoc (lines 49-51 at HEAD, carried over from the base) still claims the ambiguous result contains an empty comments array. The JSDoc immediately above the new pagination prose makes this the reference contract for the changed function. The one in-repo consumer (postMarkedComment, commentMarkers.js ~line 105) relies on existing.comments.length being populated for its detail: { matchCount: existing.comments.length } payload and the triageWorker error message (triageWorker.js:385-387) prints result.detail?.matchCount, so the code depends on the array being populated while the doc says it is empty. Impact is limited to misleading API documentation for future callers, not runtime behavior.

proof.summary: Static comparison of the JSDoc @returns clause against the two ambiguity return statements and the postMarkedComment consumer that reads existing.comments.length.

rawFindings.claim: Pagination makes findCommentByMarker issue ceil(totalComments/100) sequential GET requests per call, now amplified by auto_comment posting a comment for every triaged issue
rawFindings.description: The fix correctly trades API calls for correctness, but two interacting changes in this PR multiply the cost: (1) findCommentByMarker now walks every comment page until ambiguity or exhaustion instead of fetching one page, and (2) triageWorker now posts a marker-backed comment for every successfully triaged issue (triageOpts.auto_comment !== false, triageWorker.js:357 at HEAD), so findCommentByMarker runs on essentially every triage job rather than only needs_more_info/duplicate_hint cases. On issues with thousands of comments this turns each triage from 1 GET into dozens of sequential GETs, increasing latency and secondary-rate-limit exposure for the GitHub App installation. The early-exit at >= 2 matches bounds the worst case for the ambiguous path but not the common no-match/update path. This is an accepted-cost observation, not a defect; the update path stops as soon as the marker is found only if it appears before the last page.

proof.summary: Loop structure requires one request per 100-comment page until a short page; triageWorker now invokes postMarkedComment (and hence findCommentByMarker) on every triaged issue.
